title: Rigveda 9.8: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.8: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.8 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 670v-671r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.8.1-3 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 7, varga 30); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 670v
translation.original_text:
1e̱te somā̍ a̱bhi pri̱yam indra̍sya̱ kāma̍m akṣaran | vardha̍nto asya vī̱rya̍m ||
2pu̱nā̱nāsa̍ś camū̱ṣado̱ gaccha̍nto vā̱yum a̱śvinā̍ | te no̍ dhāntu su̱vīrya̍m ||
3indra̍sya soma̱ rādha̍se punā̱no hārdi̍ codaya | ṛ̱tasya̱ yoni̍m ā̱sada̍m ||
translation.text:
1OBEYING Indra's dear desire these Soma juices have flowed forth, Increasing his heroic might.
2Laid in the bowl, pure-flowing on to Vâyu and the Aṣvins, may These give us great heroic strength.
3Soma, as thou art purified, incite to bounty Indra's heart, To sit in place of sacrifice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 670v (numbered 92v by the scribe) (OPenn image 671, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.7.3 ‹agriyaḥ vṛṣā ava cakradat›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 671r (numbered 93r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.8.4 ‹kṣipaḥ hinvanti sapta dhītayaḥ›. Verses 9.8.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1ete | somāḥ | abhi | priyam | indrasya | kāmam | akṣaran | vardhantaḥ | asya | vīryam
2punānāsaḥ | camū-sadaḥ | gacchantaḥ | vāyum | aśvinā | te | naḥ | dhāntu | su-vīryam
3indrasya | soma | rādhase | punānaḥ | hārdi | codaya | ṛtasya | yonim | āsadam

translation.original_ref: RV 9.8.4-9 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 7, varga 30); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 671r
translation.original_text:
4mṛ̱janti̍ tvā̱ daśa̱ kṣipo̍ hi̱nvanti̍ sa̱pta dhī̱taya̍ḥ | anu̱ viprā̍ amādiṣuḥ ||
5de̱vebhya̍s tvā̱ madā̍ya̱ kaṁ sṛ̍jā̱nam ati̍ me̱ṣya̍ḥ | saṁ gobhi̍r vāsayāmasi ||
6pu̱nā̱naḥ ka̱laśe̱ṣv ā vastrā̍ṇy aru̱ṣo hari̍ḥ | pari̱ gavyā̍ny avyata ||
7ma̱ghona̱ ā pa̍vasva no ja̱hi viśvā̱ apa̱ dviṣa̍ḥ | indo̱ sakhā̍ya̱m ā vi̍śa ||
8vṛ̱ṣṭiṁ di̱vaḥ pari̍ srava dyu̱mnam pṛ̍thi̱vyā adhi̍ | saho̍ naḥ soma pṛ̱tsu dhā̍ḥ ||
9nṛ̱cakṣa̍saṁ tvā va̱yam indra̍pītaṁ sva̱rvida̍m | bha̱kṣī̱mahi̍ pra̱jām iṣa̍m ||
translation.text:
4The ten swift fingers deck thee forth, seven ministers impel thee on: The sages have rejoiced in thee.
5When through the filter thou art poured, we clothe thee with a robe of milk To be a gladdening draught for Gods.
6When purified within the jars, Soma, brightred and golden-hued, Hath clothed him with a robe of milk.
7Flow on to us and make us rich. Drive all our enemies away. O Indu, flow into thy Friend. Send down the rain from heaven, a stream of opulence from earth. Give us, O Soma, victory in war.
8Send down the rain from heaven, a stream of opulence from earth. Give us, O Soma, victory in war.
9May we obtain thee, Indra's drink, who viewest men and findest light, Gain thee, and progeny and food.
